sections.h2: Where do I go for property tax in Johnston County?
sections.html:
Johnston County Tax Administration sits on the second floor of the county courthouse at 207 East Johnston Street in Smithfield, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. except county holidays.

The office runs two phone lines, and which one you need depends on your question. Per the county contact page:

  • Tax Collection, 919-989-5120: bills, payment arrangements, wage garnishments, bank attachments and foreclosure policy. Mail goes to P.O. Box 451, Smithfield, NC 27577.
  • Tax Administration, 919-989-5130: listing property, valuation questions and property tax relief. Mail goes to P.O. Box 368, Smithfield, NC 27577.

The county also posts a tax office portal where you can look up bills, appraisal cards and sales. Sellers will want the appraisal card and the delinquent file, which the county refreshes on its downloads page for mortgage companies and the public.

sections.h2: What is the Johnston County property tax rate?
sections.html:
The county rate is 0.510 per $100 of value for the 2026 tax year, down from 0.520 the year before, and the county fire protection service district adds 0.115. The county posts a chart that shows the 2026 and 2025 rates side by side.

The chart also lists Kenly at 0.650, Princeton at 0.585, Wilson's Mills at 0.500, Pine Level at 0.390, Downtown Smithfield at 0.160, the Moccasin Creek service district at 0.025 and a research and training zone at 0.080. Your parcel's taxing districts come from the county GIS, so call 919-989-5130 if the districts on your bill look wrong.

For fiscal year 2026-2027 the county reports how its budget splits: education 32 percent, public safety 23 percent, human services 18 percent, general government 12 percent, debt service 10 percent and physical development 5 percent. Those shares do not include town or district spending.

sections.h2: When are Johnston County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bills are mailed in July and due September 1, with until January 5 to pay without interest. Interest starts January 6 at 2 percent for the first month and three-quarters of a percent for each month after.

The county mails the statement to the owner of record as of June 30, but it bills the person who owned the property on January 1. If a bill arrives for a house you already sold, the county tells owners to forward it to the new owner. Mortgage companies request their data directly from the tax office, and most lenders remit payment before year end, so the printed bill is a record for you.

Property owners who struggle with a lump sum can sign a payment agreement for current year taxes, which the county will accept until the bill turns delinquent. It does not take agreements on unpaid prior years. To pay:

  • By phone at 888-327-7344, with the tax year and bill number ready
  • Online through the county pay taxes page
  • By mail to Tax Collections, P.O. Box 451
  • In a secured drop box at the courthouse entrances

Vehicle tax is separate. Registered vehicles are taxed through the state tag and tax system and paid to the Division of Motor Vehicles.

sections.h2: What changed with the Johnston County revaluation?
sections.html:
Johnston County's last revaluation before the current one was in 2019, and the new values took effect January 1, 2025. They drive tax bills from the summer of 2025 until the next countywide revaluation, with exceptions such as new construction.

State law at G.S. 105-286 requires every county to reappraise at least every eight years. The county hired Pearson Appraisal Service for the work, and its own certified appraisers reviewed the results. Appraisers used aerial images, street-level images, sales data and the tax database, and they made field visits to more than 115,000 properties.

The county explains that appraised value and assessed value are the same as of the revaluation date. It also explains why an online estimate can differ from the tax office figure: automated models do not check whether a sale meets the statutory test, and the county screens sales by phone calls and visits. A foreclosure sale is analyzed carefully before it counts as market evidence, and your own purchase price may differ from market value.

You must report changes you make to a property, such as additions, demolished buildings, or fire and flood damage. Email taxoffice@johnstonnc.gov or call 919-989-5130, or note it on the January listing form.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Johnston County assessment?
sections.html:
Johnston County takes a real property valuation appeal on a county form during a set window, and the window for the 2026 cycle closed April 28, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. The county's appeals page says appeals of real property values begin in February 2027, so watch for that announcement.

Personal property works differently. The appeal form must reach the office within 30 days of the bill date, and the county lists the form on its tax forms page. Business and individual personal property use the same form.

After the county reviews your request, the next stop is the board of equalization and review, which under G.S. 105-322 is the board of commissioners unless the county names a separate board. You then have 30 days from the board's notice to go to the state Property Tax Commission under G.S. 105-290.

Listing is its own deadline. Owners must list taxable property from January 1 through January 31, and a late listing carries a 10 percent penalty on the total tax levied. Improvements from the prior year, unregistered vehicles, boats, aircraft and business assets are all reported on the listing form. A building permit does not take the place of the listing.

sections.h2: What tax relief programs does Johnston County offer?
sections.html:
Johnston County applies the three state homestead programs for 2026, and an owner receives only one of them. Ask for a Property Tax Relief Specialist at 919-989-5130 and file Form AV-9, which is posted on the county forms page.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: age 65 or totally and permanently disabled, with combined income of owner and spouse not above $38,800.
  • Circuit breaker deferment: same age or disability test, income not above $58,200, and five years of ownership and occupancy.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: a service-connected total and permanent disability or specially adapted housing benefit, with the surviving spouse also covered if unmarried.

Applications are due before June 1 of the tax year. Present use valuation for farm, forest and horticultural land is a separate program filed during the January listing period on Form AV-5. If the land leaves that program, deferred tax for the current year and the three before it comes due with interest. Builders can apply each January for an exclusion on inventory they hold for sale, for up to three years residential or five years commercial.

sections.h2: What should I know about tax due when I sell in Johnston County?
sections.html:
The county does not split or prorate taxes between buyer and seller. It bills the January 1 owner and mails the bill to the owner of record, so the division is left to your contract, broker or closing attorney.

The real property page makes the same point: transferring ownership during the year does not release the seller, and any proration at closing is a private agreement. Request a payoff from the collection office before closing if you owe back taxes, because a lien attaches to the parcel as of the listing date under G.S. 105-355.

Johnston County may assign a delinquent parcel to a private attorney for foreclosure after it tries other notices and sends a pre-foreclosure letter. Sales happen at the courthouse steps and normally start at 10:00 a.m. Bidders put down 5 percent, and an upset bid must exceed the last one by 5 percent or $750, whichever is greater, within ten days. Owners can redeem by paying taxes, interest and costs until the court confirms the sale.

sections.h2: What does Johnston County look like by the numbers?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts estimates 256,448 people in Johnston County on July 1, 2025, which is 18.7 percent above the April 2020 base. The county covers 792.02 square miles of land and counts about 99,408 housing units.

  • Owner-occupied housing rate, 2020 to 2024: 76.1 percent
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $305,600
  • Median household income: $83,384
  • Median gross rent: $1,146
  • Building permits in 2025: 3,002
  • Mean commute: 32.2 minutes

The courthouse and tax office are in Smithfield, and Clayton, Selma, Benson, Four Oaks and the other towns set their own rates on top of the county's.

faqs.q: What is the Johnston County tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: The county rate is 0.510 per $100 for 2026, down from 0.520 in 2025. A fire protection district adds 0.115, and towns add their own rates.

faqs.q: When does Johnston County property tax become late?
faqs.a: Taxes are due September 1 and become late after January 5. Interest begins January 6 at 2 percent for the first month and three-quarters of a percent each month after.

faqs.q: Does Johnston County split property tax between buyer and seller?
faqs.a: No. The county bills the January 1 owner and does not prorate, so ask your broker or closing attorney to settle the split in the closing statement.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Johnston County taxes in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, for the current year. Return a payment agreement to the collections office before the bill turns delinquent, because the county will not take agreements on unpaid prior-year taxes.

faqs.q: Who do I call about Johnston County property tax relief?
faqs.a: Call Tax Administration at 919-989-5130 and ask for a property tax relief specialist. Applications use Form AV-9 and are due before June 1.
